Plot aggregated catch as scatterpies on a Pacific basemap

plot_aggregated_catch.Rd

Aggregates catch data by location (and optionally by colour and facet variables), then plots each location as a pie chart ("scatterpie") whose radius is proportional to total catch and whose wedges show the proportional breakdown of colour_by. A size legend is added automatically, and the plot can optionally be faceted.

Usage

plot_aggregated_catch(
  aggregated_data,
  colour_by = NULL,
  facet_by = NULL,
  pie_radius = NULL,
  alpha = 1,
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  lim_buffer = 0.1,
  water_fill = "white"
)

Arguments

aggregated_data

A data frame of catch data with, at minimum, latd, lond and sum_catch_mt columns.

colour_by

<data-masked> Column used to fill and split each pie into wedges (e.g. species code). Set to NULL to omit colour splitting and plot single-colour pies.

facet_by

<data-masked> Optional column to facet the plot by (e.g. year, gear type). Defaults to NULL (no faceting).

pie_radius

Numeric scalar; multiplier applied to pie and legend circle radii. Defaults to 1.

alpha

Numeric scalar; fill transparency for the pie wedges. Defaults to 1.

xlim

Numeric vector of length 2 giving longitude limits (0–360 convention). Defaults to c(100, 292).

ylim

Numeric vector of length 2 giving latitude limits. Defaults to c(-62, 60).

lim_buffer

Numeric. Buffer around the outermost data points. Defaults to 0.1.

water_fill

Character string. Fill colour of the water.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples


agg_catch <- get_aggregated_catch(year = 2020:2023, species = c("YFT", "SKJ"))
